IYAHENC REPUBLIC OF THE PHILIPPINES DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT Francisco Gold Condominium Edsa Cor. Mapagmahal St., Diliman Quezon City LEGAL SERVICE DILG OPINION NO. 7 S. 2011 MAR 17 2011 HON. MARCELO V. DELA CRUZ, JR. Mayor, Municipality of Rizal Dear Mayor Dela Cruz, This has reference to your letter dated 04 March 201 1 requesting a certification from this Department that your act of hiring a private lawyer to represent your municipality in a pending court litigation was proper, after the Provincial Prosecutor and Provincial Legal Officer inhibited from said proceedings due to conflict of interest. Please be advised that this Department already had the occasion to rule upon this particular issue in Legal Opinion No. 59, series of 2007. Quoted hereunder are the pertinent rules relative to the employment of a private lawyer to represent a municipality, thus: "In reply thereto, please be informed that, as a general rule, a municipality cannot engage the services of a private lawyer. Only the Provincial Prosecutor (Fiscal), the Provincial Attorney or the Municipal Attorney could validly represent a municipality in all cases/complaints and legal problems involving it. The reason being that only accountable public officers may act for and in behalf of public entities and that public funds should not be expended to hire private lawyers (Ramos vs. Court of Appeals, 269 SCRA 34). Thus, in the case of Ramos vs. Court of Appeals, 108 SCRA 728, the Supreme Court was rather emphatic when it declared that a private lawyer cannot represent a local government unit even if the services rendered was gratis, and stated that "the municipality should not be burdened with expenses of hiring a private lawyer and that interests of the municipality would be best protected if a government lawyer handles its litigation." "However, in the case of Edgar Mancenido, et al. vs. Court of Appeals (330 SCRA 419), the Supreme Court enumerated several exceptions to the general rule discussed above, to wit: (1) Only when the provincial fiscal is disqualified may the municipal council be authorized to hire the services ofa special attorney; (2) The provincial public prosecutor is disqualified from representing a particular municipality: (a) when the jurisdiction of a case involving the municipalities lies with the Supreme Court; (b) when the municipality is a party adverse to the Provincial government or to some other municipality in the same province; and (c) when in a case involving the municipality, the provincial prosecutor, his spouse, or his child is involved as a creditor, heir, legatee or otherwise; (3) In resolving whether a local government official may secure the services of a private counsel in an action filed against him in his official capacity, the nature of the action and the relief sought are to be considered. In Albuera vs. Torres (102 Phil. 21 1 [1 9571), the Supreme Court approved the representation by

2 private counsel of a provincial governor sued in his official capacity, wherel the complaint contained other allegations and a prayer for moral damages, which, if due from the defendants, must be satisfied by them in their private capacity." Based on the foregoing pronouncements of the Supreme Court, it is the position of this Department that your act of hiring a private lawyer to handle the cases filed against you in your official capacity as the Municipal Mayor of Rizal was appropriate and in accordance with law and relevant jurisprudence. According to the documents furnished this Department, all necessary efforts wpre exerted by your good office in order to get hold of the services of a lawyer coming from the government. Being a fourth class municipality with no Legal Officer, you sought thé assistance of the Provincial Prosecutor and Provincial Legal Officer, but both lawyers begged off, citing conflict of interest as reason therefor. Your request to the Office of the Solicitor General likewise having been denied, you were then obliged to hire a private lawyer after seeking legislative authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan to defend your good office in suits to which you were charqed in your official capacity. Thus, it is clear that having no other legal recourse, your act of hiring a privhte lawyer, upon prior authorization from the Sangguniang Bayan, was justified under the circUmstances. The inhibition of both the Provincial Prosecutor and Provincial Legal Officer can bd likened to a disqualification of said government lawyers to represent the Municipality of Rizal, and therefore should be considered as an exception to the rule on non-employment of a private lawyer in accordance with the Mancenido ruling. We hope that we have addressed your concern accordingly. Very truly yours, .J SUSBDQ IV Directo II
